{{verse|chapter=10|verse=22}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Mach. 4, 56. 59.''}}* And {{sup|‖}} the Dedication vvas in Hieru{{ls}}alem: and it vvas vvinter. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=23}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Wene{{ls}}day in Pa{{ls}}sion weeke.}}And {{sc|Iesvs}} vvalked in the temple, in Salomons porche. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=24}} The Ievves therfore compa{{ls}}sed him round about, and {{ls}}aid to him, Hovv long doe{{ls}}t thou hold our {{ls}}oule in {{ls}}u{{ls}}pē{{ls}}e? if thou be {{sc|Christ}}, tel vs openly. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=25}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}wered them, I {{ls}}peake to you: and you beleeue not. the vvorkes that I doe in the name of my Father, they giue te{{ls}}timonie of me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=26}} but you doe not beleeue, becau{{ls}}e you are not of my {{ls}}heepe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=27}} My {{ls}}heepe heare my voice: and I knovv them, and they folovv me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=28}} And I giue them life euerla{{ls}}ting: and they {{ls}}hal not peri{{ls}}h for euer, and no man {{ls}}hal plucke them out of my hand. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=29}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ An other reading is, ''My father that hath giuen me, &c''.}}∷ My father, {{sup|‖}} that vvhich he hath giuen me, is greater then al: and no man can plucke them out of the hand of my father. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=30}} I and the Father are c {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ c vnum.}}∷ one.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=31}} The Ievves tooke vp {{ls}}tones, to {{ls}}tone him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=32}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered them, Many good vvorkes I haue {{ls}}hewed you from my father, for vvhich of tho{{ls}}e vvorkes doe you {{ls}}tone me? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=33}} The Iewes an{{ls}}vvered him, For a good vvorke we {{ls}}tone the not, but for bla{{ls}}phemie, and becau{{ls}}e thou being a man, make{{ls}}t thy {{ls}}elf God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=34}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered them, Is it not vvritten in your lavv, that ''I {{ls}}aid, you are goddes''?{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''P{{ls}}. 81, 6.''}} {{verse|chapter=10|verse=35}} If he called them goddes, to vvhom the vvord of God vvas made, and the {{ls}}cripture can not be broken: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=36}} vvhom the Father hath {{ls}}anctified and {{ls}}ent into the vvorld, {{ls}}ay you, That thou bla{{ls}}pheme{{ls}}t, becau{{ls}}e I {{ls}}aid I am the {{ls}}onne of God? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=37}} If I doe not the vvorkes of my father, beleeue me not. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=38}} But if I doe, and if you vvil not beleeue me, beleeue the vvorkes: that you may knovv and beleeue that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.⊣ {{verse|chapter=10|verse=39}} They {{ls}}ought therfore to apprehend him: and he vvent forth out of their handes.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=40}} and he vvent againe beyond Iordan into that place vvhere Iohn vvas baptizing fir{{ls}}t: and he taried there. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=41}} and many came to him. and they {{ls}}aid, That Iohn in deede did no {{ls}}igne. But al things vvhat{{ls}}oeuer Iohn {{ls}}aid of this man, vvere true. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=42}} And many beleeued in him.
